discovery: Experimental demonstration of fractional (anyonic) exchange statistics in the fractional quantum Hall effect

nominees.name: Gwendal Fève
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire de Physique de l'Ecole Normale Supérieure, Paris, France

motivation: Anyons, particles in two dimensions obeying statistics intermediate between bosons and fermions, were predicted theoretically in the 1970s and 1980s and linked to the fractionally charged quasiparticles of the fractional quantum Hall effect. For four decades their exchange statistics remained unobserved. Rosenow and collaborators showed how the statistics would appear directly in current cross-correlations when anyons collide at a quantum point contact. Fève and co-workers realised this anyon collider in 2020 and measured a statistical phase consistent with theta = pi/3 at filling 1/3. In the same year, Manfra's group, building on their exceptionally clean GaAs heterostructures, observed discrete phase slips in a Fabry-Perot interferometer that revealed the same braiding phase. Together these complementary experiments established anyons as physical reality, confirmed topological order as an organising principle of matter, and opened the experimental route toward non-Abelian anyons and topological quantum computation.
